newsitem.title: UK: Unilever shares up, results top forecasts.
newsitem.headline: Unilever shares up, results top forecasts.

text.p: Shares in Anglo-Dutch foods and consumer products group Unilever rose on Friday after second quarter profits beat analysts best expectations.
The shares rose 37p to 18.06 stg by 0814 GMT.
"The underlying pretax number was very good though the sales growth was poor," said one specialist salesman. "But on the whole we were encouraged by the comments in the statement."

At constant rates of exchange, the company revealed sales growth of just one percent, whilst analysts were anticipating at least double that. Meanwhile, net profit excluding the Speciality Chemicals sale rose 25 percent to 843 million stg, compared with analysts forecasts of 720-780 million stg.

The company also proposed a four-for-one stock split but analysts were disappointed that Unilever failed to say how it planned to spend the 3.02 billion stg one-off gain from the sale of its chemicals division.
"We remain cautious on Unilever and we want to know what they do with their cash-pile," said one head of market-making at a leading brokerage.
Elsewhere, analysts said they were unlikely to revise earnings forecasts significantly in light of today's results.

"Volume growth was not a great deal shy of what we were hoping for," the salesman said. "We were encouraged by the comments about investing in Latin America but were slightly worried on the outlook side."
Unilever warned that profits growth in the remainder of the year would be less buoyant.
The company said the strength of sterling and the weakness of the guilder were also likely to have a significant impact on full-year results.
"One would suspect that margins in Europe are not going to get the increases we've seen in the first half, which have been phenomenal," said the salesman.
"But we have been factoring in hits from sterling over the past six months so most people should already be expecting this."
